assessment: The sample meets neither the course-set target nor the handling-time target. Assignment changes and renames are associated with affected exports, but their causal role is unestablished. Zero observed cross-center rows does not cover the unsampled split-course case. The following capability and benefit remain hypotheses.

openings.claim: A private, week-aware course resolver could produce the documented CSV alongside a center-local checklist identifying the courses represented for that week, despite assignment changes or renames.
openings.delta: Full capability depends on stable course identities, effective-dated assignments and names, explicit split-course semantics, center authorization checks, and reads that permit concurrent attendance entry. Presently testable fragment: a staging resolver over fabricated transition histories and coordinator-agreed expected course sets; historical reconstruction in production is not assumed available.
openings.prediction: If current-state interpretation causes the affected selections, holding attendance fixed while changing assignment or name will change incumbent course membership but leave week-aware membership aligned with the agreed expectation.
openings.probe: Cap implementation and testing at six engineer-days on existing staging resources. Compare incumbent and prototype outputs for fabricated reassignment, rename, split, and cross-center identity-collision cases. Check exact expected course membership, authorized rows, documented CSV compatibility, and successful concurrent attendance entry. Stop at the prototype if production dependencies exceed the budget.
assumptions: Fabricated histories can encode coordinator-agreed week and split semantics.
A staging-only fragment fits existing hosting; production feasibility remains unverified.

openings.claim: Would an explicit expected-course checklist reduce coordinator handling, or does spreadsheet import account for most of the excess time?
openings.delta: Separates a course-verification benefit from an unobserved spreadsheet bottleneck using timed actions.
openings.prediction: If uncertainty about course coverage drives handling, the checklist will shorten checking time with little change in import time; an import bottleneck predicts little total benefit.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two sessions for counterbalanced, matched fabricated exports with and without a checklist. Time checking, correction, download, and import separately, and record course-set errors. Treat results as preliminary; assess the stated targets on the next 40 exports only after any deployment.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate ordinary spreadsheet work.
Sessions and checklist preparation share the six-day budget.
